name: Brinelock Interchange
description:
A partially submerged transit hub built into the old Chicago lakefront infrastructure where three defunct rail lines once converged. Floodwaters from Lake Michigan's risen shoreline have claimed the lower two levels entirely, leaving them as brackish warrens navigated by flatboat and submersible drone. The surviving upper tiers were converted by squatters and opportunists into a chaotic interchange point — part black market, part refugee waystation, part smuggler's dock. Corrugated walkways snake between repurposed rail cars anchored to concrete pylons, and tarp-walled stalls sell everything from gray-market Diaspora relays to unregistered BCI wipes.

The place smells like old salt and electrical burn. Ferrogate Security holds a nominal contract for the zone, but their patrols end at the waterline; everything below belongs to whoever has the better boat and the meaner crew. Carrion Logistics uses Brinelock as an unofficial waypoint for shipments too irregular to log, paying the local syndicate a tithe to keep the docks quiet. Tier 3 and 4 workers who lost housing to Lakeshore redevelopment drifted here and never left, building a strange permanent culture in the creak and drip of a place that was never meant to last.

sights: Green-brown floodwater laps at the base of rusted pylons, catching the glow of a dozen mismatched lanterns strung between rail cars.
Flatboats loaded with tarped cargo move silently through the lower corridors, their operators wearing rebreathers against the mold.
Hand-painted tier-markers are bolted to every staircase, some crossed out and rewritten three or four times over.
A rusted departure board still cycles through ghost schedules, its display half-shattered but stubbornly blinking 2:14 AM.
sounds: The constant low slap of water against concrete echoes up through the grating underfoot.
Diesel generators and hydroelectric taps create a layered hum that never fully stops, day or night.
Shouted negotiations in four or five languages overlap at the central barter deck during peak hours.
smells: Brine and algae seep up from below, mingling with fry oil from the food stalls on the upper walkway.
Ozone and solder flux drift from the electronics row where BCI jockeys run unlicensed modifications.
Wet concrete and diesel exhaust hang in the enclosed lower passages like a second atmosphere.
atmosphere.feel: Brinelock feels provisional and perpetual at the same time — a place that should have been cleared out years ago but somehow keeps pulling people back. Every surface is slightly damp. The floors vibrate faintly when the lake shifts. There is a low-grade tension that never peaks into open violence because everyone here needs the place too much to burn it down.

demographics: Predominantly Tier 3 and Tier 4 permanent residents, with a transient population of smugglers, unlicensed couriers, and displaced workers cycling through. Ethnic and national backgrounds are widely mixed, with significant East African, South Asian, and Great Lakes regional communities.
economy: Barter and gray-market Φ dominate, with Carrion Logistics providing the largest single source of liquid currency through dock fees and offload contracts. Secondary income comes from unlicensed BCI services, stolen resale, and informal ferrying between the flooded lower levels.
power_structure: A loose syndicate called the Tidemen controls dock access and enforces a rough peace, collecting tithe from every stall; Ferrogate Security maintains a surface checkpoint but cedes all real authority below the flood line.
dangers: The flooded lower levels are structurally unstable — entire sections collapse without warning, swallowing boats and people alike.
Tidemen enforcers shake down newcomers aggressively, and disputes over dock fees escalate quickly.
Unregistered BCI modifications sold here frequently carry embedded surveillance payloads from unknown third parties.
Carrion Logistics occasionally sanitizes witnesses to irregular shipments; bodies surface in the outer basin every few weeks.
opportunities: Carrion Logistics' unlisted manifests pass through here — someone with access to those records could name their price to the right buyer.
The flooded lower levels contain intact pre-flood infrastructure including sealed server vaults and armored transit lockers that have never been breached.
The Tidemen are quietly looking for outside muscle to challenge a Ferrogate Security push to extend their patrol zone below the waterline.
story_hooks: A Carrion Logistics mid-manager has gone missing somewhere in the lower levels after reportedly discovering a discrepancy in a shipment manifest. His employer wants the manifest — not the man. His family wants the man.

A sealed transit locker recovered from the sub-flood level contains a pre-collapse Axiom Industries prototype that multiple parties are now moving to acquire simultaneously, and the Tidemen who found it have no idea what they're sitting on.

A Tier 2 investigative journalist has embedded in Brinelock under a false identity to document Ferrogate's extralegal operations — but someone burned her cover, and now she needs extraction before the next patrol sweep.
frequented_by: Carrion Logistics couriers and dock crews
Displaced Tier 3-4 residents and long-term squatters
Unlicensed BCI technicians and gray-market brokers

notable_locations.name: The Departure Board
notable_locations.description: The old main concourse, now a barter floor under a cracked glass ceiling; the malfunctioning schedule board has become an unofficial community bulletin.

notable_locations.name: The Sub-Deck
notable_locations.description: The topmost flooded level, accessible by ladder at low-lake; used for private exchanges that need to happen away from Tidemen eyes.
